classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught 180° rotation about the origin to each supplied branch, carrying marked coordinates and the filled endpoint to their images.

content.prompt: Sketch the second half of these graphs so they are odd.

spec.description: Upper semicircle from the origin to (2,0), with dashed guides to (1,1). The left half-plane remains available for drawing.

answer.short: Add the lower semicircle from $(-2,0)$ to $(0,0)$, with minimum $(-1,-1)$.
answer.worked: Rotate the given arc 180° about the origin. The points $(2,0)$ and $(1,1)$ become $(-2,0)$ and $(-1,-1)$.

spec.description: Rotated lower semicircle completing the supplied graph.
spec.mathematics: Image of the supplied arc under (x,y)↦(−x,−y).

spec.description: Curve from the origin into quadrant II through (−1,1), with an outward arrow and dashed guides.
spec.mathematics: Square-root-shaped supplied branch; y=√(−x) is used to reconstruct the visible shape, not as an additional given.

answer.short: Add the matching branch in quadrant IV through $(1,-1)$.
answer.worked: Rotate the given branch 180° about the origin. The marked point $(-1,1)$ becomes $(1,-1)$. The new branch starts at the origin and continues downwards to the right.

spec.description: Right-hand parabolic branch through (0,0) and (2,0), with minimum (1,−1), dashed guides and an upward arrow.
spec.mathematics: Given branch reconstructed as y=(x−1)²−1 for x≥0.

answer.short: Add the rotated left-hand branch with maximum $(-1,1)$ and intercept $(-2,0)$.
answer.worked: Rotate the branch 180° about the origin. The minimum $(1,-1)$ becomes a maximum at $(-1,1)$, and $(2,0)$ becomes $(-2,0)$. Continue the new branch downwards to the left.

spec.description: Rotated parabolic branch in the left half-plane.
Reciprocal-shaped branch in quadrant III, approaching both axes without touching them; no numerical ticks.
spec.mathematics: Representative y=0.5/x branch for x<0; coefficient is not a supplied numerical given.

answer.short: Add the matching reciprocal-shaped branch in quadrant I, approaching both axes.
answer.worked: Rotate the given branch 180° about the origin. Its image lies in quadrant I and approaches the positive axes. Neither branch meets the origin.

spec.description: Matching branch in quadrant I with arrows at both ends.
spec.mathematics: Rotated reciprocal-shaped branch; axes remain asymptotes.

spec.description: Smooth trough from filled endpoint (−π,0) to the origin, minimum (−π/2,−1), with dashed guides and exact labels.
spec.mathematics: Sine-shaped supplied segment reconstructed as y=sin x on [−π,0].

answer.short: Add an upper arch from $(0,0)$ to a filled endpoint at $(\pi,0)$, with maximum $(\frac{\pi}{2},1)$.
answer.worked: Rotate the trough 180° about the origin. The minimum $(-\frac{\pi}{2},-1)$ becomes the maximum $(\frac{\pi}{2},1)$, and the filled endpoint $(-\pi,0)$ becomes a filled endpoint at $(\pi,0)$.

spec.description: Upper sine-shaped arch ending at a filled point at (π,0).
Curve begins at the origin with a horizontal tangent and rises increasingly steeply into quadrant I; no numerical ticks.
spec.mathematics: Representative parabolic-shaped branch y=0.6x² for x≥0; no numerical rule is supplied.

answer.short: Add the rotated branch in quadrant III, joining smoothly at the origin.
answer.worked: Rotate the given curve 180° about the origin. The new branch extends downwards to the left, with the same shape and a horizontal tangent at the origin.

spec.description: Rotated branch extending from the origin into quadrant III.
spec.mathematics: Exact rotational image of the reconstructed supplied branch.
